utterances.text: Now I want to talk about other paramilitary units, not the JNA, not the TO, not SDS units per se. Did your preparation for the report reflect the existence of relations between some of the Crisis Staffs and various volunteer or paramilitary units?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The military picture is further complicated by the fact that there were various kinds of paramilitary units. Some came from elsewhere; some formed -- from outside Bosnia; some from other parts of Bosnia also operating. But we do see contacts and cooperation between municipal Crisis Staffs and paramilitary units from outside the municipality who came to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Let me take you to tab 139 in the presentation binder, master tab 122.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a report from the Bijeljina police station to the Minister of the Interior. I'll just check the date. It's -- no obvious date, but it's following a dispatch from the minister of 9 April 1992. So it's reporting on the situation in Bijeljina. That's just the dating there on the first paragraph. But on page 2 of the translation, a third --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us where that is in the B/C/S?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Does that copy in Sanction seem to be fairly --

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the Sanction copy is very hard to read. The translation is based on, I think, actually looking at the original document, which is more legible than the electronic version. It is on page 00749560, starting about six lines from the top. But the English is a lot clearer. On page 2 in the translation, third paragraph, it says -- talking about the events on the 31st of March, 1992: "During the night and the following day, the Territorial Defence, the Serbian National Guard, and the Serbian Volunteers Guard began to lift the blockade of the town under the guidance of the Crisis Staff of Bijeljina municipality." In this context, I might recall, then, the report of the Crisis Staff of Bijeljina, dated the 1st of April, 1992, which we've seen as an example of reporting. The forces mentioned here, the Serbian National Guard and the Serbian Volunteers Guard, were paramilitary units. The Serbian National Guard was led by Ljubisa Sava, known as Mauzer, and the Serbian Volunteers Guard were led by Arkan, Zeljko Raznatovic. And it says that they took over the town under the guidance of the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And for our next document, I don't believe we have this up in Sanction. Tab number 40 -- 140 in the presentation binder is master tab 463. Can you tell us what this is and --

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's simply to identify -- to provide an identification for Mauzer's Serb National Guard.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And what is that document?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a report on paramilitary formations in the territory of the Serbian Republic of BiH, from 28 July 1992. I included it merely for reference. I don't use it otherwise.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Tab 141 in the presentation, master tab 438.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is information on the training of Arkan's volunteers by the -- from the security department of the general staff of the army of Yugoslavia, from May 1993. Similarly, I included it just to identify the Serb Volunteer Guard as Arkan's forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just for reference.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And does that document also identify any other members of Arkan's group who we talk about --

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. It identifies, in the bottom paragraph on page 1 of the translation, or the third paragraph in the B/C/S, it makes reference to the major known as Legija, who is commander of the training centre in Erdut and the commander of the Super Tigers. We'll be hearing an intercept with Legija. So just to identify him in advance as a leading member of Arkan's Serb volunteer guards.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Tab 142 in the presentation, master tab number 238. How does this pertain ...

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an order to pay out money. It's from the provisional government of Zvornik. As I note in my report, Zvornik was an exception in that there was a Crisis Staff but at the time of the takeover, shortly after the takeover in Zvornik, it created a provisional government. This is the only municipality in which I see the term "provisional government." But it was -- it replaced the Crisis Staff and acted in a matter consistent with the Crisis Staffs and War Presidencies we've seen. There was no other organ calling itself the municipal government. This was the municipal government at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And what was the date of that document, and what was its purpose?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the 4th of May, 1992, and it's an order to pay out money for the use of the needs of the special unit, the volunteers from Loznica. And the money will be taken over by the commander of the union Zuca. He was a notorious paramilitary commander in Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: So it shows that the temporary government is paying a special unit of volunteers, led by Zuca.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And related to that, tab 143 in the presentation, master tab 49. Can you tell us what that --

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is a series of documents showing the charges, and then a bill and that it's being paid, from a bus driver. On page 2 of the translation, which is 01328425 in the B/C/S, this is a bill for the transportation of volunteers on the route from Belgrade to Zvornik. So a bus driver is charging the provisional government for his transporting volunteers.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. The next one I want to talk about is an intercept, and I think you have identified three separate excerpts that you want to discuss in connection with this one. It's dated the 15th of May, 1992, and involves a person named Legija, Arkan, and another unidentified individual.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's a very long conversation in which Legija, as we saw, who is a -- one of Arkan's commanders -- commanders of one of Arkan's forces, calling in to the Erdut training centre, reporting on what he's been doing in Ilidza. And then he later talks to Arkan himself, again, describing his cooperation with the Ilidza Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And can you tell the Judges and Defence where we're starting the first excerpt?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's, I think, maybe starting on page 4 of the -- yes, starting on page 4 of the translation, and then we will go to - there are three excerpts so it's going to be a little complicated - page 7 of the translation, and later page 13.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Let's start with the first segment.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Legija: All the things he said, forget about it. That was not adopted, we came here and started organising things on our own initiative, you know. Unknown male: Yes, yes. Legija: He did not hook us up with anyone. I hooked up with the Crisis Staffs here in Ilidza and I organised everything, barracks, mobilisation, training. And yesterday during the attack when the first casualties occurred, everything became completely disorganised and discipline broke down. Unknown male: Yes, yes. Tell me, who controls Ilidza now? Legija: Our men still control Ilidza. Unknown male: Ours? Legija: Yes."

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Any comment on that first segment?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just that he connected with the Crisis Staff in Ilidza. It will be, as we see, a series of conversations. There will be more. The extent of his cooperation with the Crisis Staff will be seen.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And what unit was he associated with at the time?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Arkan's Serb Volunteer Guards.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: The second segment begins in the English on what page?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Seven.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Can you direct Mr. Krajisnik to the approximate place on the B/C/S hard copy? I'm sorry, I don't have it marked in my ...

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I don't have it marked in this copy since I just got the copy. It's at the bottom of 03290472 to the top of the following page, 0573.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: We'll play that one now.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Legija: You understand, but when the first casualties occurred, can you imagine that amid the fighting there the peasants stole the car, our car and fled. Unknown male: What did they do? Legija: They took our car, the car we got from the Crisis Staff, do you understand? Unknown male: Took it?"

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: So he got a car from the -- Arkan's soldiers got a car from the Crisis Staff in Ilidza.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And the next segment?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe page 13 -- 13 in the translation. It starts on 03290476 in the B/C/S, the sixth box from the top.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: If we can play that one.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Legija: Secondly, here in Ilidza, I, we got to Ilidza. I hooked up with ... Zeljko RAZNATOVIC: Speak louder, I can't hear you. Legija: I hooked with their Crisis Staff. Zeljko RAZNATOVIC: Aha. Legija: And then I had to split up that Crisis Staff, because some politicians and some warriors and who knows who, were interfering, so I transferred that military staff to us. Zeljko RAZNATOVIC: Aha. Legija: And I organised mobilisation and set up two barracks and started with the training and all."

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: So he's reporting to -- Legija here is reporting to Zeljko Raznatovic, Arkan, that he hooked up with, connected with, the Crisis Staff in Ilidza. And then we can see in his description of the Crisis Staff the way some Crisis Staffs were combining political and military functions, because he says he had to split up the Crisis Staff. "Some were politician and some were warriors. And he transferred the military command to us." So he saying -- I take this to mean that the Crisis Staff had some amateurs, that he had to split up, make a division of labour between the political and military, and as a military man, he set up the military command.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm about to start a new section. I don't know if there were any other administrative matters you wanted to deal with in the last three minutes, but this would be a good point for me to break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have no administrative matters in mind, but I wouldn't mind having an earlier break since I understand Mr. Petrov is not available any later than 2.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, does that mean we might be able to sort out this issue today? Because each day it arises in practice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: So before Mr. Krajisnik leaves this building.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, whether it will be before he leaves this building is another matter. I'm available immediately now to briefly discuss the matter. I also do understand that -- I misunderstood that Mr. Petrov said he had a meeting at 2.00 and therefore would not be available. Of course, we have some information. Mr. Hannis, it might be -- well, I don't think at this moment that we need your assistance in resolving the matter. If you would not mind that I discuss the matter with Mr. Stewart --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I don't mind at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: I told Mr. Hannis what the issue was, Your Honour, which seemed perfectly reasonable, so that the Prosecutor didn't feel there was some mystery that I wasn't sharing with them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We'll see whether we can resolve the matter. But this is all none of your concern, Ms. Hanson. I would like to give you the same instructions I gave you yesterday, that is, not to speak about the testimony you have given and the testimony you're still about to give. You have an idea now as well how much time it will take, approximately. It's expected to take until at least next week, Tuesday. And we'd like to see you back tomorrow morning at 9.00, in the same courtroom. We'll adjourn until tomorrow morning, 9.00, courtroom II.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 3rd day of March, 2005, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.43 p.m.,
